turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we won't be wasting time. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, so tell me who decided that, and why nobody called me first.
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No. I asked you a question, Hale: who entered the zero before anyone called me?
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Don't manage me, Hale. If he's one of your favourites, then explain to me why he learned about a zero from the gradebook, sitting in front of his classmates.
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.

"Aren't perfect." Even the company that sells that checker says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have their guide printed in my bag. So what else do you have, or is a machine's guess the entire case?
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.
I'm writing that down: 11:31, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58. What date, Hale, and whose account is that file under? Turn the screen so I can read it myself.
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
Flattery won't do it, Hale. The screen, and the date on that file, or I'm going upstairs to see the principal.
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not here to grade you, Hale. The zero comes off, I get an apology, and you've still never shown me that screen.
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.
I'm writing that down too. A misquoted line costs a student marks, Hale, but it doesn't earn him a zero. Show me the page where it appears, alongside that version history, with the date on it.
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.

"Completely different direction" is an adjective, Hale, and I don't take adjectives as evidence. Different in what way, exactly: the thesis, the argument, which scenes he used? You now have three documents in this room and I haven't seen a single page of any of them.
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? I have a client call at 4:40 and my son has a zero, Hale. Owen.
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.

Ten minutes left. I'm writing down "nothing goes on his record," and I'll want that in an email, with the principal copied. But offering a rewrite means you think something is wrong with the essay, Hale, and I still haven't seen a single page that shows it.
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
You're asking me how to do your job, Hale? You'll speak to Owen once the zero is off and I've read those documents myself, not before.
